summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Entry routes: Porogamy (micropyle, most common), Chalazogamy (chalaza), Mesogamy (integuments). Double fertilization (S.G. Nawaschin, 1898): (1) Syngamy: 1st male gamete (n) + Egg (n) -> Zygote (2n), and (2) Triple Fusion: 2nd male gamete (n) + 2 Polar Nuclei (2n) -> Primary Endosperm Nucleus PEN (3n).

conceptBreakdown.content:
Pollen-Pistil Interaction encompasses all dynamic dialogue events from pollen deposition on the stigma up to pollen tube entry into the embryo sac.

### 6.1 Pollen Tube Entry Routes

```
                        POLLEN TUBE ENTRY ROUTES
                                    │
         ┌──────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────┐
         ▼                          ▼                          ▼
     POROGAMY                   CHALAZOGAMY                MESOGAMY
  Enters via Micropyle       Enters via Chalaza         Enters via Integuments
  (Most common angiosperms)  (Casuarina, Juglans)       or Funicle (Cucurbita)
```

- Regardless of the ovule entry route (Porogamy, Chalazogamy, or Mesogamy), the pollen tube **ALWAYS enters the Embryo Sac through the Micropylar end** by penetrating one of the degenerate Synergids via the **Filiform Apparatus**.

### 6.2 The Double Fertilization Event (S.G. Nawaschin, 1898)

$$\text{Syngamy: } n \text{ (male gamete)} + n \text{ (egg)} \longrightarrow 2n \text{ (zygote)}$$

$$\text{Triple Fusion: } n \text{ (male gamete)} + 2n \text{ (polar nuclei)} \longrightarrow 3n \text{ (PEN)}$$

conceptBreakdown.heading: LURE Chemotropic Peptides
conceptBreakdown.title: LURE Chemotropic Peptides
conceptBreakdown.content: Synergids secrete cysteine-rich defensin-like polypeptides called LURE peptides that act as species-specific chemotropic attractants, binding receptor-like kinases (RLKs) on the pollen tube tip to guide directional growth.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Degenerating Synergid Discharge
conceptBreakdown.title: Degenerating Synergid Discharge
conceptBreakdown.content: The pollen tube tip bursts inside one of the synergids upon contact, releasing its two non-motile male gametes and tube nucleus directly into the synergid cytoplasm.
